## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible branchless blend for the particle update loop can approach the streaming ceiling by eliminating per-particle branches and enabling compiler vectorization.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill (N≈963) lies below all measured points. The L2 spill (N≈61680) falls between N=10000 and N=100000. At q=0.01, cost FALLS monotonically from 6.322 ns/p (N=10000, L2-resident) through 5.298 (N=100000, just past L2 spill) to 4.709 (N=10M, DRAM-resident) — no knee at the L2→DRAM transition, only continued overhead amortization. The roughly 200-instruction Halide buffer-struct setup on the stack (str/stp to sp before `bl _halide_b2`) is fixed cost that dominates at small N and washes out by N=10M. Death rate reshapes the floor without changing the N-trend: q=0.25 is perfectly flat (4.767→4.708 ns/p) and fastest overall, while q=0.5 raises the floor to ~5.43 ns/p with backend_stall climbing from 24.3% (N=10000) to 43.2% (N=10M).

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 14.44 GB/s at N=10M, q=0.01 (matched by 14.43 at q=0.1 and 14.44 at q=0.25) — 48% of the 29.9 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound at small N (10.76 GB/s = 36% of ceiling at N=10000, q=0.01) and transitions to a compute/backend-bound regime at large N, never reaching bandwidth-bound status. At q=0.5, bandwidth drops to 12.52 GB/s (42% of ceiling) and backend_stall reaches 43.2% at N=10M versus 28.9% at q=0.01, indicating memory latency from scattered byte writes dominates at high churn. The 15.5 GB/s gap to ceiling is never closed at any measured regime.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the per-particle loop. Only 2 vector-suffixed instructions appear in 353: `movi.2d v1` (zero a register) and `uqadd.8b v4, v4, v3` (one saturating byte-add on a fast path). The core computation is entirely scalar: `ldp s4, s5` loads two floats, then `fadd s4`, `fmul s4` (×2), `fcvtzs w0`, `fsub s4`, `fmul s4` (×2), `fcvtzs w1` — all single-element. An indexed load `ldr d3, [x12, x14, lsl #3]` performs a per-particle table lookup, not a cross-particle gather. The render section performs byte-granular scatters: repeated `ldrb`/`add`/`csel`/`strb` sequences writing individual bytes to an image buffer at computed offsets. The 77 `str` and 35 `stp` instructions are dominated by Halide buffer-struct marshaling on the stack before `bl _halide_b2`. This codegen explains the 48% ceiling: scalar per-particle math caps compute throughput, and byte-granular scatter stores cannot stream.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 14.44 GB/s (48% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling) at any N or death rate. The compiler emitted only 2 vector instructions and kept the per-particle math scalar (`fadd s4`, `fmul s4`, `fcvtzs`), while the render loop's byte-granular `strb` scatters prevent streaming. The Halide buffer setup overhead (77 `str` + 35 `stp`) further suppresses small-N performance to 10.76 GB/s. The branchless blend is Halide-expressible but neither vectorized nor bandwidth-efficient.
